metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to 'all contributions'; disclosure triggered when AI used for 'substantive portions' of the contribution (no numeric/volume threshold given)
domains.accountability_wording: Contributors are responsible for all submitted content, regardless of whether generative AI tools were used.

evidence.quote: Contributors are responsible for all submitted content, regardless of whether generative AI tools were used.
If generative AI tools were used for substantive portions of the contribution, contributors must describe their use in the change description.
Contributors must be able to explain all changes during review.

domains.reasoning: Policy explicitly names contributions, requires disclosure for substantive AI use, requires contributors be able to explain changes (human-in-the-loop element), and assigns accountability to the contributor by name. Both supervision and accountability holder are stated.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The document is entirely about generative AI use in contributions and never mentions meetings, recordings, or notetaker bots.

evidence.quote: In the context of Generative AI, this particularly means conveying information (comments, documentation, etc) in a style the Astropy community uses, and that is appropriate and to the point.

domains.suggested_improvement: no explicit supervision level or accountability holder stated for documentation/content specifically
domains.reasoning: Documentation is named as an example under the general 'consistency with conventions' rule, but no distinct supervision level or accountability statement is given for content/documentation as its own category, and blogs/design assets are never mentioned. This is reached mainly through the general contribution rules rather than a dedicated content rule.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI-assisted moderation actions or who is accountable
domains.reasoning: The policy does not discuss AI use in moderation decisions (e.g., closing/banning contributors); the only related clause ('we will close the PR' for agent-driven submissions) is an enforcement mechanism attached to the autonomous-use rule, not a moderation-domain rule.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on whether/how AI may be used to review contributions
domains.reasoning: The policy discusses reviewers only in the context of expecting to interact with a human contributor; it never addresses reviewers or maintainers themselves using AI tools to conduct reviews.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to autonomous workflows/agents acting on the repository (e.g., opening/interacting with PRs)

evidence.quote: Autonomous workflows ("agents") are not human contributors. Astropy reviewers expect to interact with the human controlling the account, or we will close the PR.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder named; 'will close the PR' is enforcement, not authorship responsibility
domains.reasoning: The policy clearly bans unsupervised agentic interaction with the repository (supervision level = banned), naming the area explicitly. However it states only who enforces the ban (reviewers closing PRs), not who is accountable for autonomous-generated output, so accountability_holder is not_specified and the domain is only partially addressed per the metric's yes-bar.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of energy, water, or carbon impact of AI tools
domains.reasoning: The policy never raises environmental cost as a concern or rule; it focuses solely on contributor accountability, disclosure, engagement, and style.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware/financial cost from AI use
domains.reasoning: No statement in the document addresses infrastructure strain, hardware cost, or financing related to AI tool use.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on whether project content/user data may train models
domains.reasoning: The policy addresses licensing responsibility for submitted code but never discusses whether Astropy's own project data (issues, discussions, contributions) may be used to train AI models.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Astropy's AI policy is narrowly and specifically written for code/PR contributions (permitting AI-assisted contributions under disclosure, human-explainability, and contributor-accountability rules, and banning fully autonomous agent interaction), but it is silent on notetaker bots, dedicated content/documentation rules, moderation, AI-assisted review, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and use of the project's own data for training.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
